ayahs.textEnglish: OH, THE LAYING-BARE of the truth!
How awesome that laying-bare of the truth!
And what could make thee conceive what that laying-bare of the truth will be?
THE LIE gave [the tribes of] Thamud and ‘Ad to [all tidings of] that sudden calamity!
Now as for the Thamud - they were destroyed by a violent upheaval [of the earth];

ayahs.textArabic: وَاَمَّا عَادٌ فَاُهْلِكُوْا بِرِيْحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۙ
ayahs.textEnglish: and as for the ‘Ad - they were destroyed by a storm wind furiously raging,

ayahs.textArabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَّثَمٰنِيَةَ اَيَّامٍۙ حُسُوْمًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيْهَا صَرْعٰىۙ  كَاَنَّهُمْ اَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Sakhkharahā ‘alaihim sab‘a layāliw wa ṡamāniyata ayyām(in), ḥusūman fataral-qauma fīhā ṣar‘ā, ka'annahum a‘jāzu nakhlin khāwiyah(tin).
ayahs.textEnglish: which He willed against them for seven nights and eight days without cease, so that in the end thou couldst see those people laid low [in death], as though they were so many [uprooted] trunks of hollow palm trees:
and dost thou now see any remnant of them?

ayahs.textArabic: وَجَاۤءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَنْ قَبْلَهٗ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكٰتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa jā'a fir‘aunu wa man qablahū wal-mu'tafikātu bil-khāṭi'ah(ti).
ayahs.textEnglish: And there was Pharaoh, too, and [many of] those who lived before him, and the cities that were overthrown - [all of them] indulged in sin upon sin

ayahs.textArabic: فَعَصَوْا رَسُوْلَ رَبِّهِمْ فَاَخَذَهُمْ اَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
ayahs.textLatin: Fa ‘aṣau rasūla rabbihim fa akhażahum akhżatar rābiyah(tan).
ayahs.textEnglish: and rebelled against their Sustainer's apostles: and so He took them to task with a punishing grasp exceedingly severe!

ayahs.textArabic: اِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا الْمَاۤءُ حَمَلْنٰكُمْ فِى الْجَارِيَةِۙ
ayahs.textEnglish: [And] behold: when the waters [of Noah's flood] burst beyond all limits, it was We who caused you to be borne [to safety] in that floating ark,

ayahs.textArabic: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَّتَعِيَهَآ اُذُنٌ وَّاعِيَةٌ
ayahs.textLatin: Linaj‘alahā lakum tażkirataw wa ta‘iyahā użunuw wā‘iyah(tun).
ayahs.textEnglish: so that We might make all this a [lasting] reminder to you all, and that every wide-awake ear might consciously take it in.

ayahs.textArabic: فَاِذَا نُفِخَ فِى الصُّوْرِ نَفْخَةٌ وَّاحِدَةٌ ۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Fa iżā nufikha fiṣ-ṣūri nafkhatuw wāḥidah(tun).
ayahs.textEnglish: Hence, [bethink yourselves of the Last Hour,] when the trumpet [of judgment] shall be sounded with a single blast,

ayahs.textArabic: وَّحُمِلَتِ الْاَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَّاحِدَةًۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa ḥumilatil-arḍu wal-jibālu fa dukkatā dakkataw wāḥidah(tan).
ayahs.textEnglish: and the earth and the mountains shall be lifted up and crushed with a single stroke!
And so, that which must come to pass will on that day have come to pass;
and the sky will be rent asunder - for, frail will it have become on that Day -;

ayahs.textArabic: وَّالْمَلَكُ عَلٰٓى اَرْجَاۤىِٕهَاۗ وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَىِٕذٍ ثَمٰنِيَةٌ  ۗ
ayahs.textLatin: Wal-malaku ‘alā arjā'ihā, wa yaḥmilu ‘arsya rabbika fauqahum yauma'iżin ṡamāniyah(tun).
ayahs.textEnglish: and the angels [will appear] at its ends, and, above them, eight will bear aloft on that Day the throne of thy Sustainer’s almightiness…

ayahs.textArabic: يَوْمَىِٕذٍ تُعْرَضُوْنَ لَا تَخْفٰى مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
ayahs.textLatin: Yauma'iżin tu‘raḍūna lā takhfā minkum khāfiyah(tun).
ayahs.textEnglish: On that Day you shall be brought to judgment: not [even] the most hidden of your deeds will remain hidden.

ayahs.textArabic: فَاَمَّا مَنْ اُوْتِيَ كِتٰبَهٗ بِيَمِيْنِهٖ فَيَقُوْلُ هَاۤؤُمُ اقْرَءُوْا كِتٰبِيَهْۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Fa ammā man ūtiya kitābahū biyamīnihī fa yaqūlu hā'umuqra'ū kitābiyah.
ayahs.textEnglish: Now as for him whose record shall be placed in his right hand, he will exclaim: "Come you all!" Read this my record!
Behold, I did know that [one day] I would have to face my account!
And so he will find himself in a happy state of life,
in a lofty paradise,
with its fruits within easy reach.

ayahs.textArabic: كُلُوْا وَاشْرَبُوْا هَنِيْۤـًٔا ۢبِمَآ اَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى الْاَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ
ayahs.textLatin: Kulū wasyrabū hanī'am bimā aslaftum fil-ayyāmil-khāliyah(ti).
ayahs.textEnglish: [And all who are thus blest will be told:] "Eat and drink with good cheer in return for all [the good deeds] that you have sent ahead in days gone by!"

ayahs.textArabic: وَاَمَّا مَنْ اُوْتِيَ كِتٰبَهٗ بِشِمَالِهٖ ەۙ فَيَقُوْلُ يٰلَيْتَنِيْ لَمْ اُوْتَ كِتٰبِيَهْۚ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa ammā man ūtiya kitābahū bisyimālih(ī), fa yaqūlu yā laitanī lam ūta kitābiyah.
ayahs.textEnglish: But as for him whose record shall be placed in his left hand, he will exclaim: "Oh, would that I had never been shown this my record,
and neither known this my account!
Oh, would that this [death of mine] had been the end of me!
Of no avail to me is all that I have [ever] possessed,
[and] all my power of argument has died away from me!"
Thereupon the command will go forth:] "Lay hold of him, and shackle him,
and then let him enter hell,

ayahs.textArabic: ثُمَّ فِيْ سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُوْنَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوْهُۗ
ayahs.textLatin: Ṡumma fī silsilatin żar‘uhā sab‘ūna żirā‘an faslukūh(u).
ayahs.textEnglish: and then thrust him into a chain [of other sinners like him - a chain] the length whereof is seventy cubits:

ayahs.textArabic: اِنَّهٗ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللّٰهِ الْعَظِيْمِۙ
ayahs.textEnglish: for, behold, he did not believe in God, the Tremendous,
and did not feel any urge to feed the needy:
and so, no friend has here today,

ayahs.textLatin: Wa lā ṭa‘āmun illā min gislīn(in).
ayahs.textEnglish: nor any food save the filth
which none but the sinners eat!"
BUT NAY! I call to witness an that you can see,
as well as all that you cannot see!
Behold, this [Qur’an] is indeed the [inspired] word of a noble apostle,

ayahs.textArabic: وَّمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍۗ قَلِيْلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُوْنَۙ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa mā huwa biqauli syā‘ir(in), qalīlam mā tu'minūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: and is not – however little you may [be prepared to] believe it - the word of a poet;

ayahs.textArabic: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍۗ قَلِيْلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُوْنَۗ
ayahs.textLatin: Wa lā biqauli kāhin(in), qalīlam mā tażakkarūn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: and neither is it - however little you may [be prepared to] take it to heart - the word of a soothsayer:
[it is] a revelation from the Sustainer of all the worlds.
Now if he [whom We have entrusted with it] had dared to attribute some [of his own] sayings unto Us,
We would indeed have seized him by his right hand,
and would indeed have cut his life-vein.

ayahs.textArabic: فَمَا مِنْكُمْ مِّنْ اَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حٰجِزِيْنَۙ
ayahs.textEnglish: and none of you could have saved him!
And, verily, this [Qur’an] is a reminder to all the God-conscious!

ayahs.textLatin: Wa innā lana‘lamu anna minkum mukażżibīn(a).
ayahs.textEnglish: And, behold, well do We know that among you are such as will give the lie to it:
yet, behold, this [rejection] will indeed become a source of bitter regret for all who deny the truth [of God's revelation] –
for, verily, it is truth absolute!
Extol, then the limitless glory of thy Sustainer's mighty name!
